transcriptSegments.text: People say, I am honest, as if honesty is something you own, like the color of your
eyes, like your height, like a trophy you once won and keep forever.
But that is not how honesty works.
Nobody says, I am the sport I play.
You play sport, you practice, you lose, you learn, you get better and honesty.
Honesty is no different, you play honesty.
Every day, every conversation, every mistake, every moment, reality says,
you are wrong.
And then comes the question, do you defend yourself or do you change?
Because honesty is not staying.
I was always right, honesty is saying, I thought this, I learned that and now I think
something closer to true.
That is not weakness, that is growth, that is courage, because the goal of life is
not to become someone who never changes.
The goal is to become someone who changes well, a compass is not faithful, because
it never moves.
A frozen needle is not loyal to north, it is only stuck.
The needle keeps faith with north by moving, turn and the needle swings back every time.
And maybe honesty is exactly that, I never change, but I keep turning toward
what is real.
Someone who can look reality in the eye and say, teach me again and again.
Because honesty is not who you are, it is how you become, how you become whole.
